items.title: Add federated actor identity and agent credentials
items.body:
Axxium now represents humans and agents as separate actor kinds, reserves the configured administrator email for verified Google sign-in, and lets administrators issue expiring, revocable agent credentials. A verified AT Protocol OAuth callback can sign in or link a hosted DID; reciprocal handle/DID resolution remains a lookup rather than an authentication grant.

The production image contains only runtime dependencies and the compiled server, while `open-hax/services` owns the PDS and ingress. Locally, Axxium and Knoxx run under PM2 with Google OIDC and the shared account manager.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Sign in with Google or an AT Protocol identity, and link an AT Protocol identity to an existing account.
  * System administrators can create agents, issue time-limited credentials, review credentials, and revoke them.
  * Administrators can look up AT Protocol identities and manage actors and their capabilities.
  * The account portal provides sign-in options, actor details, identity linking, and administrative tools.
* **Security**
  * Sign-up enforces password requirements and reserves the configured administrator email for federated sign-in.
  * Administrative features are restricted to system administrators.
  * Cross-origin requests are limited to the configured public address, and the application container runs as a non-root user.

items.title: Support independent cross-host identities and service environments
items.body:
Axxium can now copy a signed identity from one host instance to another. The browser portal registers accounts, requires password reauthentication for export, copies a five-minute recipient-bound Ed25519 transfer, and imports it once with a new recipient password. Actor/entity IDs survive; sessions, passwords and permissions remain local. Issuer public keys are explicitly pinned, and account conflicts fail closed.

This also repairs PostgreSQL parameter/session handling and exposes actor data only to the authenticated actor. The isolated non-root compose runtime has separate database state and secrets per host. The environment workflow calls the immutable Services controller for code-owner testing leases and main-merge staging; CODEOWNERS names the existing repository admins.

Validation: warning-free compile and release build; 5 tests / 20 assertions; boundary check; 28 real HTTP/database assertions; actual browser registration, clipboard transfer, recipient registration and fresh Yoga login while Stealth's Axxium container was stopped. Browser screenshots are retained in the operator acceptance artifacts. No production deployment was performed.

Activation requires this workflow and CODEOWNERS to reach main. Testing/staging keys and isolated receiver slots are already installed; Services controller is pinned to f9bfe1724a662930fc10fcb9ba0f46eac78fbc52.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Added an identity portal for account creation, sign-in, logout, and account details.
  - Added secure identity export and import between configured Axxium instances.
  - Added host preparation and Compose-based deployment with persistent PostgreSQL storage.
  - Added automated testing and staging environment promotion workflows.

- **Security**
  - Added stronger session, transfer-token, password, and request protections.
  - Restricted account and entity access to the signed-in account.

- **Documentation**
  - Expanded setup guidance for hosted environments, identity transfer, verification, and deployment.
